full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of renal tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows proximal convoluted tubules exhibiting changes characteristic of acute cellular injury, including loss of brush borders, cell swelling, and vacuolization. Some tubular lumens contain cellular debris and casts. These findings are typical of acute tubular necrosis.

random.description: This is a light micrograph of kidney tissue stained with H&E, showing the renal cortex and tubules. The tubular epithelial cells exhibit degenerative changes, including cytoplasmic swelling and vacuolization. These histological findings are characteristic of acute tubular necrosis, a common cause of acute kidney injury. The interstitium and surrounding structures show typical morphological alterations associated with ischemic or toxic tubular damage.
